label: Whatever depends for its being on what depends on z depends on z
paraphrase: OPEN analyst premise: if x depends for its being on y and y depends for its being on z, then x depends for its being on z. Stated separately from reflexivity and from nonmutuality, about DependsForBeing as DEF-DEPENDS-FOR-BEING defines it (no closure of the relation is meant). Challenge: counterfactual dependence is not transitive in general (Lewis's logic invalidates counterfactual transitivity, which is why Lewis takes causation as the ancestral of dependence), so the premise fails for D if D is mere counterfactual dependence. Candidate warrant: per se ordered composition, as in the Second Way's 'the first is the cause of the middle and the middle of the last': if x depends for its being on y only as receiving it through y's own dependence on z, x depends on z. Neither is established here.
